title: Stolen LEGO Technic McLaren MCL39 sets recovered after train heist
summary: 123 copies of LEGO Technic 42228 McLaren MCL39, worth close to $30,000, were stolen from a cargo train in California and have since been recovered by local police.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to Brick Fanatics, 123 copies of the LEGO Technic 42228 McLaren MCL39 set were stolen from a BNSF cargo train in San Bernardino County, California. The set, released in March, retails for £199.99 in the UK.

The Barstow Sheriff's Department says a deputy spotted an abandoned van packed with large boxes and recovered the stolen sets on Monday. BNSF Railway confirmed the boxes contained the missing LEGO sets and thanked the deputy for the find.

No suspects have been named and the investigation is ongoing, with these thefts reportedly linked to a wider string of cargo train burglaries in the area.

## Why it matters
While this is a US story, it's a reminder of just how valuable big Technic sets have become - a single haul here was worth nearly $30,000. For UK collectors and F1 fans eyeing the MCL39, it also highlights how in-demand licensed motorsport sets can be, both with builders and, unfortunately, thieves.

## What to watch next
It's worth keeping an eye out for any update on arrests or further details on the string of train burglaries mentioned by police, as well as whether any of the recovered sets end up affecting stock or pricing for the MCL39.

title: LEGO Ideas: Gilmore Girls fan build hits 10,000 votes
summary: A reworked Gilmore Girls LEGO Ideas project, designed by BrickinNick, has passed the 10,000-vote threshold and will be considered in LEGO's second Ideas review of 2026.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A fan-designed LEGO Ideas project based on Gilmore Girls, called *Gilmore Girls: Life in Stars Hollow*, has reached the 10,000-vote milestone needed for LEGO Group review consideration, according to Brick Fanatics.

The build recreates familiar Stars Hollow locations including Luke's Diner, Lorelai's House, and the Town Sign and Gazebo, currently shown in a winter setting, though the designer says it could be adapted for other seasons. It includes nine minifigures: Lorelai Gilmore, Luke Danes, Rory Gilmore, Lane Kim, Emily Gilmore, Kirk, Taylor Doose, the Town Troubadour, and Jess Mariano.

This is designer BrickinNick's third project to hit 10,000 votes, following an earlier Gilmore Girls version (which qualified in January 2025) and a Cybertruck submission — neither of which was picked up by LEGO. The set will now be one of 79 (and counting) projects considered in LEGO's second Ideas review of 2026.

Reaching 10,000 votes only means a project earns a review — it's not confirmation LEGO will produce it as an official set. Still, it's an encouraging step for fans of the show, and shows how persistence on LEGO Ideas can pay off, as seen recently with 21372 La Catrina, which also began as a fan submission before becoming a real set.

## What to watch next
The review window closes in just over two weeks. If BrickinNick's Gilmore Girls build is selected, LEGO would then need to confirm it as an official product — something that hasn't happened yet, so this remains firmly speculative at this stage.

title: LEGO 1989 Batmobile vs 1992 Batmobile: how the new set compares
summary: LEGO DC has officially revealed 76355 Batman Returns Batmobile, and Brick Fanatics has compared it against 2019's 76139 1989 Batmobile to see what's changed in size, price and design.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO DC has officially unveiled 76355 Batman Returns Batmobile, the first LEGO version of the sleek black car from Tim Burton's 1992 film, which splits apart to reveal the Batmissile. It's being treated as a spiritual successor to 76139 1989 Batmobile, released back in 2019.

Comparing the two sets: the new 76355 measures over 10cm high, 45cm long and 17cm wide, with 2,269 pieces at £189.99 / $229.99 / €209.99. The older 76139 is bigger and pricier, at over 12cm high, 60cm long and 22cm wide, with 3,308 pieces for £219.99 / $249.99 / €249.99.

Design-wise, the new model reportedly smooths out exposed studs from the front of the older car with tiles, though it swaps back to smaller rear wheels. Side pipework has been refreshed with more protruding grey pieces, exhaust vents look rounder, and the windshield appears slightly taller. The size and piece count reduction seems to come with a trade-off in detail and fewer minifigures, though the new set reportedly gains one notable extra feature not detailed in this excerpt.

## Why it matters
Batmobile sets are a big deal for LEGO DC collectors, and direct comparisons like this help fans decide whether the new smaller, cheaper set is worth it compared to the larger original. It's also a useful look at how LEGO's design and engineering approach to vehicle sets has evolved over seven years.

title: LEGO designer reveals the tricky part of building Pokémon's Arcanine
summary: The senior designer behind LEGO's 72160 Arcanine has spoken about the design process, admitting the Fire-type's face was the toughest part to get right.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Senior Designer Dan Squirrell has given an insight into how 72160 Arcanine, a 1,190-piece LEGO Pokémon set, came together. Speaking to LEGO.com, he explained that translating Arcanine's rounded, organic Pokémon shapes into square LEGO bricks meant focusing on overall silhouette before adding detail, starting with rough sketches to nail the 'macro shapes'.

According to Squirrell, the trickiest element by far was the face. He said getting it right at such a small scale was 'a real engineering challenge', but crucial, since fans would spot any mistakes instantly.

The set launched on 1 August 2026 as part of a wider wave of LEGO Pokémon releases, many of which include SMART Play interactive elements. Arcanine notably doesn't feature that tech, putting the focus squarely on its build and display appeal instead.

## Why it matters
For builders and collectors, this kind of behind-the-scenes detail is a useful look at how official LEGO designers tackle organic, characterful shapes using standard bricks — techniques that are just as relevant to custom and compatible-brick model makers aiming for similar likenesses.

## What to watch next

title: Is this LEGO's first ever 'display-only' minifigure?
summary: The new 76355 Batman Returns Batmobile features a Michael Keaton Batman figure whose draped cape locks his arms and legs in place, sparking debate over whether it's the first minifigure built purely for display.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has spotted something unusual in the upcoming LEGO set 76355 Batman Returns Batmobile: a new Michael Keaton Batman minifigure design. Instead of the usual rubber cape-and-cowl piece seen in earlier sets like 76139 1989 Batmobile, this version drapes a moulded cape fully around the figure's body.

While that looks great for recreating the character's iconic pose, it comes at a cost. The cape doesn't just stop head movement like before – it also restricts the arms and legs from turning at all. According to the report, there may be a tiny bit of wiggle room if you get fingers underneath the cape, or a slight tilt at the waist when the figure is fixed to studs, but proper posing looks off the table. The set includes a display stand, suggesting this Batman is designed to be placed and admired rather than played with.

## Why it matters
Minifigures are usually prized for their flexibility – you can pose them, swap parts, and use them in your own builds. A figure that's essentially locked into one dramatic stance is a first for many collectors, and it raises questions about where LEGO might be heading with future licensed, display-focused sets. For collectors and display-build fans, it's a sign that highly detailed sculpting is sometimes being prioritised over playability.

## What to watch next
The set hasn't been released yet, so it's worth checking hands-on reviews once 76355 Batman Returns Batmobile is available to see exactly how much (if any) articulation the figure retains. It'll also be interesting to see whether this approach appears in other upcoming licensed sets.

title: LEGO Icons Star Trek USS Enterprise Bridge reviewed: modular set scores 8/10
summary: Brick Fanatics has published its review of LEGO Icons 11385, the 1,701-piece modular USS Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge set, praising its display options and minifigures but flagging fiddly instructions and heavy sticker use.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has reviewed LEGO Icons 11385 Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge, an 18+ set with 1,701 pieces (a nod to the ship's registration number). It's a modular playset recreating the original 1960s-style bridge, following on from last year's 10356 U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701-D.

The set is built around a C-shaped base with angled wall-mounted computer stations, plus separate modules for the captain's chair, helm console, viewscreen and turbolift. Reviewers compared its construction style to the 2016 LEGO Star Wars Carbon-Freezing Chamber set, sharing a similar grey, black and orange colour scheme.

The review awarded the set 8/10 overall, with strong marks for playability, value and minifigures (9/10 each), but a lower design score (7/10). Praised points included the unique modular design, multiple play/display configurations and near-perfect crew minifigures. Criticisms included unclear building instructions, an excessive number of stickers, and a suggestion that a transporter room element should have been offered as a gift-with-purchase instead.

## Why it matters
This is only the second LEGO Icons Star Trek set, so it's an important signal for how far LEGO Group is willing to expand this newer licensed theme. For fans of TV/film-based Icons builds and modular display sets, it's a useful early verdict before committing to the purchase.

title: LEGO releases behind-the-scenes documentary for The X-Files Ideas set
summary: A new official LEGO documentary explores the design of 21369 The X-Files, focusing on the tricky triangular UFO build.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has released an official documentary-style video covering the design of the recently launched LEGO Ideas set 21369 The X-Files. Published on LEGO.com as part of the ongoing 'Secrets of our Sets' series (which appears to be replacing the older LEGO Designer Videos format), it follows a similar release for 11377 The Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith.

The video digs into the challenges of recreating the set's UFO element, which designer Chris McVeigh describes as a genuinely tough build due to its perfect triangular shape - something LEGO elements aren't typically suited to. To solve it, the team reused a technique involving the golden ring element as a spacer to lock the sides to the centre, previously used on 10289 Bird of Paradise.

The documentary also explains why the UFO doesn't spin, despite that seeming like an obvious play feature. Designers say this was a deliberate choice for accuracy to the show, since that craft type doesn't rotate in flight, and adding a spin mechanism would have required cross-axles and gears that would compromise the set's transparent display stand.

## Why it matters
For fans and collectors, these documentaries offer a rare look at the real design decisions and building techniques behind official LEGO Ideas sets, which can be genuinely useful inspiration for custom builders and MOC creators tackling awkward geometric shapes.

Watch for whether LEGO continues rolling out 'Secrets of our Sets' documentaries as a regular feature for future Ideas and Icons releases.
